title: Lending & Flash-Funding Arbitrage — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Escrow-Locked Double Closes, Earnest-Money Qualification, Liquidity Velocity, Wire Controls, State Lending Reviews, and Small-Team Operating Discipline

worksheets.title: Arbitrage Deal / Counterparty Underwriting & Spread Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Qualify each proposed advance before promising liquidity. Establish the actual repayment source, verify every counterparty independently, and separate earned fees from principal movement. Reject apparent spreads that depend on provisional buyer funds, unsecured reimbursement promises, or unverified settlement instructions.
instructions: Assign one immutable deal identifier before reviewing documents. Map the seller-to-intermediary purchase and intermediary-to-end-buyer resale separately, then identify which obligations require cash, which documents create repayment rights, and which parties can change settlement instructions.

Obtain the complete purchase agreements, resale agreement, settlement agent engagement, and proposed disbursement schedule. Compare legal names, property identifiers, dates, assignment restrictions, and cancellation rights rather than relying on a broker summary or proof-of-funds letter.

Verify the settlement agent through independently sourced contact information and confirm applicable bonding, insurance, licensing, and underwriter relationships. Record evidence dates and limits; a familiar logo or prior successful transaction does not authenticate new wire instructions.

Require unconditional end-buyer cash on deposit before releasing principal to the verified bonded title or settlement agent. Treat lender commitments, pending transfers, conditional deposits, and screenshots as insufficient; document the agent's written confirmation and its precise limitations.

Calculate spread after capital usage, verification work, settlement charges, and reserves. Apply the same cash-release requirement to earnest-money proposals; ordinary speculative deposits fail this playbook when the required end-buyer cash cannot already be verified.

fields.name: Deal identity and transaction chain
fields.prompt: Record the immutable deal identifier, property description, contracting entities, settlement sequence, and proposed advance. Explain exactly where the operator enters the chain and which agreement establishes the right to receive repayment.
fields.example: Deal LF-030-001 concerns 18 Cedar Avenue. Cedar Buyer LLC purchases for $100,000 and resells to Harbor Holdings LLC for $125,000. The operator advances $100,000 only to the verified settlement account; a signed funding agreement directs return of principal plus a $2,000 earned fee.

fields.name: Counterparty identity and signing authority
fields.prompt: Identify each entity's registration, beneficial ownership evidence, authorized signer, and independently verified contact route. Distinguish identity checks from creditworthiness and document inconsistencies that must be resolved before any commitment becomes executable.
fields.example: Cedar Buyer LLC provides its state registration, operating agreement, manager resolution, and signer identification. The analyst matches the manager across all four records and calls a previously verified number. A different email domain triggers fresh verification rather than an automatic update to payment instructions.

fields.name: Settlement agent qualification
fields.prompt: Document the settlement agent's applicable license, bond, insurance, bank account title, and title-underwriter relationship. Capture independently sourced verification evidence, including exclusions that could prevent recovery after escrow theft or unauthorized disbursement.
fields.example: The proposed agent presents a $250,000 fidelity bond and $1 million errors-and-omissions policy. The analyst verifies status with the issuer and checks whether lender loss and employee dishonesty are covered. The $100,000 advance remains blocked until account ownership and applicable settlement authority are independently confirmed.

fields.name: Unconditional end-buyer cash evidence
fields.prompt: Describe the evidence proving end-buyer cash is already deposited, available for the specified closing, and free of unresolved funding conditions. Identify the agent providing confirmation and any remaining contractual right that could interrupt disbursement.
fields.example: Harbor deposits $125,000 into the verified escrow account before release. The settlement officer confirms receipt, availability, and satisfaction of buyer funding conditions in writing. A pending ACH credit does not qualify. The reviewer also checks cancellation language because deposited cash alone does not eliminate contractual withdrawal risk.

fields.name: Repayment waterfall and instruction priority
fields.prompt: Specify the order of principal return, earned fee payment, settlement expenses, and intermediary proceeds. Reconcile the waterfall against both closing statements and identify whose written acceptance makes the disbursement instructions operationally effective.
fields.example: The resale receives $125,000. Accepted instructions allocate $100,000 to principal return, $2,000 to the operator's earned fee, $3,000 to other settlement expenses, and $20,000 to Cedar. Both transactions must balance independently; the operator's $100,000 initial advance pays the first purchase price and is never fee revenue.

fields.name: Net spread qualification
fields.prompt: Calculate the transaction's earned fee less attributable capital, verification, transfer, and administration costs. State the minimum acceptable contribution and distinguish this deal-level result from annual owner profit after overhead and portfolio losses.
fields.example: A $2,000 funding fee less $80 capital cost, $150 diligence, $50 wire charges, and $120 administration produces $1,600 transaction contribution. The contribution ratio is 80%, but the canonical base annual owner margin remains 42.5% after all modeled operating expenses and loss-related costs.

fields.name: Earnest-money structure qualification
fields.prompt: Describe whether the proposed earnest-money arrangement creates repayable debt, genuine shared investment risk, or another economic relationship. Evaluate actual loss allocation and the universal cash-release condition instead of accepting a promotional product label.
fields.example: A sponsor requests $15,000 of earnest money for a promised $3,000 profit split, but no end-buyer cash is deposited. The request is rejected under this operating policy. Calling the arrangement a Gator joint venture does not cure missing repayment evidence or resolve state lending characterization.

fields.name: Corporate promotional-credit suitability
fields.prompt: Record the issuer's permitted transaction types, promotional period, transfer charges, repayment requirements, and cash-advance treatment. Explain how funds would reach escrow without disguised purchases, unsupported representations, or dependence on repeated credit extensions.
fields.example: An issuer offers a documented promotional transfer with a 3% charge. Moving $20,000 costs $600 before any escrow expense. A proposed $500 earned fee therefore loses at least $100. The operator rejects the transaction rather than treating a 0% promotional interest rate as costless liquidity.

fields.name: Failure triggers and exposure limits
fields.prompt: List transaction-specific rejection triggers, maximum principal exposure, expected settlement duration, and concentration limits. Identify the person who can stop funding when evidence changes and the records required to resume the review.
fields.example: LF-030-001 has a $100,000 principal ceiling and a planned two-business-day cycle. Changed beneficiary details, conditional buyer cash, missing bond verification, or unsigned repayment instructions stop release. The owner may restart review only after independent evidence resolves the specific failure; commercial pressure cannot substitute for verification.

fields.name: Underwriting decision and evidence expiry
fields.prompt: Summarize the decision, outstanding conditions, evidence timestamps, and validity window. Separate a preliminary indication from an executable commitment, and explain which document changes require complete re-underwriting rather than a clerical amendment.
fields.example: The preliminary indication allows $100,000 for a $2,000 fee, subject to same-day cash and beneficiary verification. It expires after three business days. A new buyer, settlement agent, property, or repayment waterfall requires a fresh decision. Only the owner signs the final commitment after the reviewer completes all evidence checks.

worksheets.completion_gate: Advance only when all ten underwriting records identify their evidence, the verified bonded settlement agent has accepted repayment instructions, unconditional end-buyer cash is confirmed, and the owner records an explicit executable commitment within its validity window.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Escrow/Reserve Float & Working-Capital Calculator
worksheets.purpose: Build a capital model that distinguishes fee revenue, deployed principal, protected reserves, and available borrowing capacity. Reproduce the three canonical annual scenarios exactly, then test whether settlement duration, funding charges, concentration, and fixed expenses support the proposed operating cadence.
instructions: Copy the canonical annual revenue, margin, profit, and staffing figures without substituting transaction contribution for owner profit. Derive total modeled costs by subtraction, and keep principal movement outside every revenue calculation and sales dashboard.

Build a fee bridge using completed services and enforceable compensation terms. Separate transactional fees, earned origination points, and any retained joint-venture economics; do not count the same compensation twice because it appears on multiple settlement documents.

Model peak deployment using actual settlement calendars, bank cutoffs, holidays, and overlapping commitments. Use business days for capacity planning and the contractual day-count convention for capital charges; disclose the difference whenever weekends extend cash usage.

Ring-fence operating and loss reserves before offering commitments. Treat external facilities as available only after execution and satisfaction of draw conditions, and never use another client's escrow funds to bridge an unrelated transaction or operating expense.

Stress the model for delayed repayment, disputed fees, unavailable facilities, and principal impairment. Reconcile transaction ledgers to bank evidence and the annual scenario, then state whether the startup capital supports the planned capacity without assuming unlimited recycling.

fields.name: Canonical scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter all three canonical annual scenarios with revenue, owner margin, owner profit, derived total costs, and staffing. Explain that these are modeled annual outcomes rather than closing-day cash balances or automatic results.
fields.example: Conservative: $120,000 revenue, 30% margin, $36,000 owner profit, $84,000 costs, one full-time operator plus two contractors. Base: $535,000, 42.5%, $227,375, $307,625, identical staffing. Scaled: $950,000, 55%, $522,500, $427,500, two full-time staff plus three contractors. Each profit equals revenue multiplied by its stated margin.

fields.name: Recognized fee revenue bridge
fields.prompt: Construct an illustrative annual fee mix that reconciles exactly to each scenario. Identify service completion and contract evidence for earned amounts, exclude returned principal, and distinguish origination compensation from duplicated funding fees.
fields.example: Conservative uses 60 completed closings at $2,000, totaling $120,000. Base uses 250 at $2,000 plus 35 separately earned $1,000 origination fees, totaling $535,000. Scaled uses 450 at $2,000 plus 50 separately earned $1,000 origination fees, totaling $950,000. Each additional origination fee requires distinct contractual support.

fields.name: Principal and retained-share classification
fields.prompt: Define principal, operator-owned fees, and compensation collected for others. Document principal-versus-agent treatment for fees within ASC 606 and identify lending amounts requiring other accounting guidance instead of forcing all receipts into one category.
fields.example: A $102,000 receipt contains $100,000 principal and $2,000 earned operator compensation. Principal reduces the advance receivable. For a separate agency arrangement collecting a $3,000 fee with retained_share of 0.40, recognized operator revenue is $1,200 and $1,800 is payable onward. That illustration does not increase canonical revenue.

fields.name: Startup capital and committed capacity
fields.prompt: Allocate startup cash between protected reserves and deployable equity, then identify executed external capacity separately. Show the maximum simultaneous principal commitment and the consequences if a proposed facility is unavailable at launch.
fields.example: At the $100,000 startup ceiling, protect $50,000 and deploy $50,000 of equity. A hypothetical executed $450,000 facility would create $500,000 total deployment capacity. Without that facility, capacity remains $50,000 and the illustrated $100,000 deal cannot proceed; promotional credit limits do not automatically replace committed funds.

fields.name: Capital turns and deployment utilization
fields.prompt: Calculate annual principal throughput, principal-days, average deployment, and utilization using explicit assumptions. Distinguish capacity arithmetic from achievable demand, and leave room for settlement bunching rather than scheduling every dollar continuously.
fields.example: Base throughput assumes 250 closings at $100,000, or $25 million of principal movement, not revenue. Two business days per closing creates $50 million principal-days. Across 250 business days, average deployment is $200,000, representing 40% utilization of $500,000 capacity. Five simultaneous $100,000 deals consume all capacity.

fields.name: Per-deal contribution and capital charge
fields.prompt: Itemize one transaction's earned fee and direct costs, including the actual capital-charge convention. Compute contribution before fixed overhead, and identify whether minimum facility charges or unused-line fees require additional annual expense allocations.
fields.example: For LF-030-001, $2,000 revenue less $80 capital, $150 diligence, $50 transfers, and $120 administration leaves $1,600. The $80 capital charge assumes $100,000 for two chargeable days at 14.6% on an actual/365 basis. A weekend extension or facility minimum requires recalculation before the quote remains valid.

fields.name: Base annual cost bridge
fields.prompt: Reconcile illustrative direct costs and recurring overhead to the canonical base total cost envelope. Show each category separately and explain whether monthly operating expenses exclude transaction-linked capital charges, contractor work, or portfolio provisions.
fields.example: Base costs comprise $100,000 closing direct costs, $7,000 separate origination delivery costs, $120,000 recurring overhead, $50,000 additional portfolio capital costs, and $30,625 loss-related expense. Total costs equal $307,625, leaving $227,375 from $535,000 revenue. Recurring overhead averages $10,000 monthly, within the stated $2,000–$12,000 operating range.

fields.name: Protected reserve and liquidity runway
fields.prompt: Set an operating reserve, loss buffer, and minimum available cash floor. Explain reserve ownership and replenishment rules, and distinguish an earmarked cash balance from a booked loss expense so the model avoids double counting.
fields.example: The protected $50,000 comprises $30,000 for three months of $10,000 recurring overhead and $20,000 of loss liquidity. Earmarking does not itself create an expense. The annual $30,625 loss-related budget is separate from reserve cash, and new commitments stop if projected unrestricted cash falls below the required operating floor.

fields.name: Delay and impairment sensitivity
fields.prompt: Quantify an extended settlement and a principal-loss case separately. State additional capital costs, unavailable capacity, and incremental profit impact relative to the canonical base; do not silently replace the published scenario with stressed results.
fields.example: Three extra chargeable days on $100,000 add $120 at 14.6% actual/365 and occupy one funding slot longer. Separately, a $25,000 incremental loss beyond all modeled provisions reduces base owner profit from $227,375 to $202,375. Neither stress result changes the canonical $227,375 scenario printed in the scorecard.

fields.name: Owner distributions and cash reconciliation
fields.prompt: Specify when earned profit may be distributed after bank reconciliation, payable settlement, reserve replenishment, and facility obligations. Explain why revenue recognition, accounting profit, collected fees, and distributable cash can differ during growth.
fields.example: The monthly review shows $40,000 earned revenue, $23,000 expenses, and $17,000 accounting profit, but $5,000 of fees remain uncollected. Collected operating surplus is $12,000 before other balance-sheet changes. The owner defers distributions until contractor payables, facility requirements, and the $50,000 protected reserve are fully covered.

worksheets.completion_gate: Proceed only after all three scenarios reproduce their exact canonical profits, the fee bridge excludes principal, the reserve and external capacity assumptions are explicit, and the proposed closing calendar fits available committed cash under the documented delay stress.

worksheets.title: End-to-End Execution, Idempotent Ledger & QA Pre-Flight Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Translate underwriting into a controlled settlement process with independent wire verification, explicit state transitions, and replay-safe records. Preserve a complete principal and fee trail while preventing duplicate releases, premature revenue posting, and silent exceptions during delayed or disputed closings.
instructions: Create separate preparation and release responsibilities even when contractors support a single full-time owner. Require independent evidence review before the bank instruction becomes executable, and log who checked beneficiary ownership, buyer cash, and accepted repayment terms.

Represent the deal as explicit operational states with permitted transitions and evidence requirements. Prevent automation from jumping directly from intake to funded, and freeze movement when a material document changes after the final pre-flight review.

Use immutable event identifiers and unique business keys for ledger operations. Persist intent before requesting a transfer, then reconcile provider status before retrying; a timeout does not prove failure and must never automatically trigger a second wire.

Reconcile both sides of every principal movement against bank records and settlement statements. Post fees only when earned under the applicable agreement and accounting policy, and keep bank availability distinct from revenue recognition and contractual collectability.

Conduct a tabletop incident before the first funded closing. Test changed wiring instructions, duplicate callbacks, delayed repayment, and an unavailable reviewer, then preserve the decision trail and correct any workflow capable of releasing cash without the required evidence.

fields.name: State machine and transition evidence
fields.prompt: List permitted deal states and the evidence required for each transition. Identify terminal rejection states, reversible preparation steps, and the point where an external payment creates an obligation that cannot be undone locally.
fields.example: LF-030-001 moves through intake, verified, documented, cash-confirmed, release-authorized, submitted, funded, repaid, and reconciled. A bank acknowledgment is required before funded status. Rejected is terminal unless a new review version is created. Once a wire is submitted, deleting an application record cannot cancel the external instruction.

fields.name: Independent beneficiary verification
fields.prompt: Describe the callback procedure, trusted contact source, account ownership evidence, and reviewer separation. Specify how changed instructions invalidate earlier verification and how the team avoids authenticating a suspicious message through that same message.
fields.example: The preparer uploads the agent's instructions, and the reviewer calls a number verified during onboarding rather than the email signature. They confirm beneficiary name, routing number, account digits, and deal reference. Any change creates a new verification record and blocks reuse of the prior release authorization.

fields.name: Release packet and final pre-flight
fields.prompt: Define the minimum release packet and its freshness requirements. Include buyer cash confirmation, signed repayment instructions, settlement-agent verification, available capital, and exact beneficiary details, with a named reviewer responsible for resolving discrepancies.
fields.example: The release packet contains both contracts, accepted disbursement instructions, current agent checks, same-day $125,000 buyer cash confirmation, and the $100,000 wire request. The reviewer compares every amount with the ledger. Missing signatures, changed buyer identity, or stale beneficiary verification returns the deal to documented status.

fields.name: Idempotency key and retry behavior
fields.prompt: Define a unique key for each intended principal disbursement and explain retry behavior after timeouts. Distinguish application deduplication from bank-side protection and require status reconciliation wherever the payment provider cannot enforce idempotent requests.
fields.example: The business key is LF-030-001:principal-release:v1. SQLite enforces one release-intent row for that key, while a separate attempt record stores provider references. A timeout moves the attempt to status-review. The operator checks the bank before retrying; application uniqueness alone cannot prevent a manually duplicated bank wire.

fields.name: Principal and fee journal entries
fields.prompt: Write balanced entries for advance, fee earning, collection, and transaction costs. Identify the supporting event for each posting and ensure principal return reduces the receivable rather than inflating earned revenue or profit.
fields.example: Advance: debit principal receivable $100,000 and credit cash $100,000. When the contractual service is complete, debit fee receivable $2,000 and credit fee revenue $2,000. Collection debits cash $102,000 and credits those receivables $100,000 and $2,000. Direct costs debit expense $400 and credit cash or payables $400.

fields.name: Escrow payoff reconciliation
fields.prompt: Specify the documents and arithmetic used to reconcile repayment against the accepted waterfall. Define tolerances, investigation ownership, and treatment of short payments without silently rewriting the original contractual fee or principal balance.
fields.example: The payoff ledger expects $102,000 but the bank receives $101,950. A $50 difference is assigned to investigation, not automatically deducted from revenue. The reviewer obtains the bank advice and settlement statement to determine whether an authorized transfer charge, underpayment, or posting error explains the discrepancy.

fields.name: Immutable evidence and version history
fields.prompt: Describe storage locations, document versions, access restrictions, and event timestamps. Explain what a cryptographic digest proves and what it cannot establish about authenticity, legal authority, or the accuracy of a settlement representation.
fields.example: Each accepted PDF receives a SHA-256 digest, UTC timestamp, document version, and uploader identity in the evidence index. Originals remain access-controlled and retained under the record schedule. Matching hashes demonstrate unchanged bytes after capture; they do not prove that the signer had authority or that buyer cash existed.

fields.name: QA fixtures and expected outcomes
fields.prompt: List deterministic test cases for duplicate requests, partial repayments, stale documents, and invalid transitions. State expected ledger balances and system behavior so a reviewer can repeat the tests before workflow changes reach production.
fields.example: Submitting the same release key twice produces one $100,000 intent. A $60,000 principal repayment leaves $40,000 outstanding. A changed beneficiary blocks release. A duplicated bank event creates no second journal entry. Tests compare exact integer-cent balances and require every accepted posting batch to balance to zero.

fields.name: Wire incident response and escalation
fields.prompt: Define the immediate response to suspected diversion, including bank contacts, evidence preservation, settlement notification, and reporting ownership. Distinguish requesting recall or cancellation from obtaining confirmed recovery of the transferred funds.
fields.example: If the $100,000 wire appears diverted, the owner immediately contacts the bank's fraud desk and requests recall, preserves headers and call records, and alerts the verified settlement agent. UCC 4A-211 cancellation depends on timing and applicable rules. The ledger continues showing exposure until recovery is confirmed.

fields.name: Closing pack and exception closure
fields.prompt: Specify the final evidence required to close a deal operationally and in the ledger. Assign unresolved exceptions an owner and deadline rather than marking the transaction complete solely because expected cash has appeared.
fields.example: LF-030-001 closes only after principal receivable reaches zero, the $2,000 fee is supported and collected, the $400 direct costs are posted, and settlement statements match the bank. A missing signed statement remains an open documentation exception with a named owner, even when the cash reconciliation is exact.

worksheets.completion_gate: Release only after the independent reviewer signs the current packet and the ledger contains one authorized release intent. Mark the worksheet complete after duplicate-event tests pass, repayment reconciles, and every remaining exception has an explicit owner.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract Addendum & Compliance Audit
worksheets.purpose: Convert jurisdictional questions into documented operating requirements before quoting or deploying capital. Evaluate licensing, interest characterization, escrow authority, referral compensation, and enforceability using actual transaction facts rather than assuming that short duration or entity borrowers create universal exemptions.
instructions: Map borrower location, property location, lender activity, solicitation channels, and settlement location before selecting governing law. Assign qualified counsel a specific fact pattern and request a written operating matrix with permitted structures and evidence requirements.

Analyze economic substance before naming a product. A mandatory repayment promise and fixed return can support lending treatment despite joint-venture terminology, while genuine investment participation requires careful review of actual control, risk sharing, and compensation.

Separate federal coverage questions from state licensing and rate restrictions. Business-purpose treatment under one federal rule does not establish a state exemption, authorize escrow activity, or validate every fee imposed on a short-duration advance.

Attach transaction-specific schedules to the funding agreement and obtain the settlement agent's acceptance of operational instructions. Confirm that contract language matches actual accounts, timing, available remedies, and the agent's authority to carry out the proposed disbursement.

Maintain a change log for laws, counsel conclusions, issuer terms, and settlement-agent requirements. Stop affected activity when a material assumption changes, then update templates, intake questions, and training before the revised structure is offered to counterparties.

fields.name: Jurisdiction and activity map
fields.prompt: Record all locations and activities relevant to lending, brokering, solicitation, and settlement. Explain why contractual governing law alone does not settle licensing or mandatory statutory requirements, and identify the reviewer responsible for each jurisdiction.
fields.example: The operator works from California, the borrowing entity is organized in Delaware, and the property and settlement agent are in Arizona. Counsel reviews both operating-state and transaction-state requirements. A Delaware governing-law clause is recorded but does not replace analysis of California lending activity or Arizona settlement authority.

fields.name: Commercial lending license analysis
fields.prompt: Identify the statute governing the proposed lending activity, the asserted exemption, and the facts supporting its use. Require a conclusion about actual transactions rather than treating commercial purpose or short duration as self-executing exemptions.
fields.example: For California activity, the review addresses the California Financing Law, including Financial Code section 22100 and applicable exemptions such as those in section 22050. The matrix records whether this operator and transaction qualify. An entity borrower and a two-day term alone do not establish an exemption.

fields.name: Interest characterization and rate review
fields.prompt: Inventory interest, origination points, extension charges, mandatory participation fees, and amounts paid to affiliates. Calculate an illustrative annualized burden, then identify the jurisdiction-specific method and exemptions used for the actual rate-limit analysis.
fields.example: A $2,000 charge on $100,000 for two days equals 2% for the period and 365% using simple 365-day annualization. That diagnostic is not a substitute for statutory methodology. California Constitution article XV, section 1, and applicable exemptions require review; renaming interest a service fee does not resolve its treatment.

fields.name: Federal business-purpose scope
fields.prompt: Document actual use of proceeds, borrower organization, collateral, and occupancy facts relevant to federal coverage. Distinguish any business-purpose exclusion from continuing state requirements and retain evidence supporting the classification for each transaction.
fields.example: The file documents an entity's purchase and immediate resale of investment property, with no personal occupancy. The review addresses 12 CFR 1026.3(a) for Regulation Z and 12 CFR 1024.5(b)(2) for Regulation X business-purpose exclusions. Changed use or borrower facts trigger a fresh scope determination rather than automatic reuse.

fields.name: Escrow authority and custody boundaries
fields.prompt: Identify who may receive, hold, and disburse the funds under applicable state rules. Record licensing or exemption evidence and keep the operator's funding role distinct from providing unlicensed settlement or escrow services.
fields.example: Where California escrow activity is involved, the review considers Financial Code section 17200 and relevant exemptions, including section 17006. The operator wires only to the verified bonded agent's designated account. It does not collect unrelated buyer deposits in its operating account or advertise itself as the escrow holder.

fields.name: Commercial disclosures and referral compensation
fields.prompt: Determine whether commercial funding disclosures or referral restrictions apply to the specific product and parties. Record compensation recipients, actual services, and statutory coverage rather than assuming every introduction can generate a lawful fee.
fields.example: California Financial Code section 22800 and following provisions are screened for applicable commercial funding disclosures and exemptions. For a covered federally related mortgage transaction, 12 U.S.C. 2607 restricts settlement-service kickbacks and unearned fee splitting. A $250 referral proposal remains unpaid until coverage and permitted compensation are documented.

fields.name: Funding agreement and settlement addendum
fields.prompt: Specify principal, earned compensation, maturity, release conditions, repayment waterfall, extension treatment, and dispute handling. Require the addendum to distinguish borrower obligations from the settlement agent's separately accepted instructions and actual authority.
fields.example: The schedule states $100,000 principal, $2,000 earned funding compensation, and a two-business-day target. Release requires verified unconditional buyer cash and accepted repayment instructions. Extensions require written terms reviewed for rate restrictions. The agent separately acknowledges the waterfall; the borrower cannot bind the agent merely by signing the funding agreement.

fields.name: Security interests and insolvency exposure
fields.prompt: Identify collateral, attachment requirements, perfection method, competing claims, and insolvency consequences. Distinguish contractual payment instructions from a perfected security interest, and document why escrow segregation does not automatically eliminate bankruptcy or priority disputes.
fields.example: Counsel reviews UCC 9-203 for attachment and 9-310 for filing requirements and exceptions where Article 9 applies. Real-property interests need separate analysis. The file also considers 11 U.S.C. 362 and 547. A signed payoff instruction alone does not establish perfected priority or make a repayment immune from avoidance litigation.

fields.name: Credit data, signatures, and record controls
fields.prompt: Document permissible credit-data access, signer authentication, electronic record retention, and access restrictions. Separate electronic-signature validity from identity verification, and assign retention periods according to applicable law and documented business requirements.
fields.example: A personal credit report requires a documented permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b. Electronic execution is evaluated under 15 U.S.C. 7001 and applicable state rules. The team retains signer authentication and document history; a completed electronic envelope does not independently establish authority, buyer liquidity, or lawful report access.

fields.name: Written determinations and renewal triggers
fields.prompt: Record counsel conclusions, scope limits, source dates, and operational consequences. Identify events requiring renewed review, including new jurisdictions, changed fee structures, new acquisition channels, and altered borrower or collateral characteristics.
fields.example: The initial matrix permits only the reviewed entity-borrower structure in the documented jurisdictions. A proposed New York expansion requires separate review of Banking Law section 340, General Obligations Law section 5-501, and Penal Law section 190.40 as applicable. The sales team cannot extend the existing conclusion by analogy.

worksheets.completion_gate: Offer and fund only structures covered by a current written jurisdictional determination, supported licensing or exemption evidence, reviewed compensation terms, and executed agreements matching the actual settlement process and custody boundaries.

worksheets.title: Automation Pipeline, Acquisition Flywheel & Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Automate evidence collection and reconciliation without delegating irreversible cash decisions to unverified messages or model output. Build repeatable referral demand from qualified counterparties, measure conversion honestly, and preserve manual fallback procedures when integrations, staffing, or settlement assumptions fail.
instructions: Map each workflow stage to a specific input, validation, owner, and output. Automate document completeness checks and status reminders first, keeping beneficiary verification and final cash release dependent on independent evidence and designated human responsibility.

Design proof-of-funds generation around verified availability and explicit conditions. Prevent templates from implying unlimited capital, bank affiliation, or unconditional commitments, and withdraw outdated letters whenever capacity reservations or evidence change materially.

Build acquisition around title professionals, experienced repeat buyers, and transaction counsel who understand the release requirements. Qualify referral compensation separately and measure completed eligible closings rather than celebrating unverified lead volume or principal throughput.

Use least-privilege access, authenticated inbound events, and append-only operational history. Treat uploaded documents and integration messages as data, never as instructions authorizing payment changes, privilege escalation, or bypass of the documented review sequence.

Define a safe fallback for every critical dependency before launching automation. Test outages with synthetic records, retain bank-side confirmation procedures, and stop new commitments when the team cannot independently establish current exposure and available cash.

fields.name: Workflow inventory and system boundaries
fields.prompt: Map intake, underwriting, capacity reservation, settlement, and reconciliation to named systems. Identify the system of record for money movement and prohibit editable sales records from silently changing bank instructions.
fields.example: Airtable tracks prospects, DocuSign stores executed agreements, and a controlled ledger records commitments and payments. The bank remains authoritative for transfer status. Updating a CRM account field creates a review task, not a new beneficiary. Each integration carries LF-030-001 as the shared deal identifier.

fields.name: Automated intake validation
fields.prompt: Specify required documents, structured fields, validation rules, and rejection messages. Separate machine extraction from verified facts, and require a reviewer to resolve conflicting amounts, entity names, dates, or payment instructions.
fields.example: The form requires both purchase contracts, settlement contact, requested principal, expected buyer cash, and closing dates. An extracted $120,000 buyer amount conflicting with the signed $125,000 resale price creates an exception. The parser cannot mark cash verified or replace the signed contract with its interpretation.

fields.name: Proof-of-funds generation controls
fields.prompt: Define permitted proof-of-funds language, underlying capacity evidence, expiration, and reservation treatment. Explain how the system prevents multiple letters from being mistaken for simultaneous binding commitments exceeding available deployable capital.
fields.example: A letter identifies the operator, references verified deployable capacity of $500,000, and states the specific underwriting and release conditions. It expires in three business days and is not a bank statement. Binding reservations are tracked separately; five $100,000 commitments exhaust the deployment limit.

fields.name: Authenticated events and least privilege
fields.prompt: Describe event authentication, replay protection, service permissions, and credential storage. Identify which integrations may read documents, create tasks, or post ledger events, and which must never initiate external transfers.
fields.example: Inbound signing events require provider-supported authentication and unique event identifiers. The document integration can create review tasks but cannot access bank release credentials. Secrets remain in a managed credential store, not CRM notes. Replayed events return the existing result without another ledger posting.

fields.name: Escrow payoff automation
fields.prompt: Define expected payoff amounts, matching keys, exception tolerances, and reviewer responsibilities. Explain how automation handles pooled receipts, short payments, duplicate bank records, and descriptions that do not uniquely identify the funded transaction.
fields.example: The matcher expects $102,000 for LF-030-001 and compares amount, verified sender, reference, and date. A $204,000 receipt cannot automatically close two deals without allocation evidence. A repeated bank event is deduplicated. Any shortfall or ambiguous reference creates a reviewer task before receivables change.

fields.name: Referral channel and value proposition
fields.prompt: Identify the target referral partners, their qualifying transaction characteristics, and the operational value offered. Exclude promises of guaranteed funding and document any proposed referral payment for separate statutory review.
fields.example: The owner contacts ten settlement firms handling repeat investor double closes. The proposition is clear eligibility, fast document review, and reliable payoff reconciliation, not payment for steering business. Partners receive a checklist requiring deposited buyer cash and accepted instructions before any funding commitment.

fields.name: Acquisition funnel and cost attribution
fields.prompt: Define each funnel stage with objective entry criteria and measure conversion through completed closings. Assign acquisition costs consistently and avoid counting the same operator time in both overhead and direct deal expenses.
fields.example: One monthly cohort contains 40 leads, 20 complete files, eight eligible deals, and four funded closings. At $2,000 per closing, earned fees total $8,000. A $1,200 incremental outreach spend produces $300 acquisition cost per funded deal. This cohort is a pilot, not the annual base forecast.

fields.name: Repeat-counterparty flywheel and concentration
fields.prompt: Describe post-close feedback, repeat eligibility, concentration limits, and counterparty monitoring. Explain why successful historical closings can reduce administrative friction without replacing fresh cash, identity, and beneficiary checks.
fields.example: After reconciliation, the owner sends the partner a one-page timing review and requests the next eligible file. No borrower may occupy more than $100,000 of the $500,000 deployment limit. Repeat status prepopulates unchanged entity documents but never waives same-day cash or wire verification.

fields.name: Dependency failure and manual fallback
fields.prompt: List critical dependencies, outage symptoms, safe manual procedures, and suspension criteria. Require fallback records to preserve unique deal identifiers and reviewer separation so later recovery does not create duplicate transfers.
fields.example: If the ledger service fails, the team stops new releases until it can reconstruct current exposure from the last verified export and bank records. A controlled manual register may support monitoring and repayment tracking. Restored events retain original identifiers and undergo duplicate checks before posting.

fields.name: Automation benefit and risk measurement
fields.prompt: Measure time saved, exception rates, false matches, and review effort against a manual baseline. Set thresholds for disabling automation when speed improves but reconciliation quality, evidence completeness, or release control deteriorates.
fields.example: A pilot reduces intake administration from 45 to 20 minutes per file. Across 40 files, that saves 1,000 minutes, or 16 hours 40 minutes. Two extraction errors are caught before review completion. Any false cash-verification status disables that automation immediately, regardless of time saved.

worksheets.completion_gate: Activate only workflows that preserve independent release verification, authenticated events, unique payment intent, and recoverable evidence. Complete the acquisition tracker with measured conversion, attributed costs, concentration limits, and a successfully rehearsed dependency outage.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod KPI Scorecard & Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Turn the first month into a sequence of verifiable operating deliverables rather than a forced funding deadline. Establish clear small-team responsibilities, track cash and exception quality, and preserve transferable records that support controlled growth, succession, or an eventual business sale.
instructions: Use the first 30 days to establish reviewed structures, verified partners, ledger controls, and qualified demand. Preserve the canonical one-to-four-month time to first deal; do not force a closing simply to satisfy a launch calendar.

Assign accountable owners for underwriting, independent verification, bank release, reconciliation, and incident response. Make contractor availability explicit and document how the operation pauses safely when reviewer coverage is absent during a scheduled closing.

Build a weekly scorecard separating earned fee revenue, principal exposure, reserve coverage, settlement duration, and unresolved exceptions. Compare actual activity with a clearly labeled ramp plan rather than presenting annual scenarios as monthly commitments.

Prepare continuity and transferability records from the beginning. Retain executed contracts, renewal dates, system ownership, and counterparty permissions, while avoiding assumptions that licenses, facilities, or referral relationships automatically transfer with an entity sale.

Finish the month with an evidence-based review of capital readiness, operating quality, and pipeline eligibility. Continue building where requirements are satisfied, but retain explicit stop conditions for missing authority, unverified cash, or insufficient liquidity.

fields.name: Days 1–7: structure and capital readiness
fields.prompt: Specify first-week deliverables for jurisdiction review, entity authority, banking access, reserve allocation, and proposed facility verification. Assign evidence owners and avoid treating an application or indicative term sheet as deployable capital.
fields.example: By day seven, the owner assembles the jurisdiction matrix request, bank signer records, and $100,000 startup allocation. The register protects $50,000 and identifies $50,000 deployable equity. A proposed $450,000 facility remains excluded from capacity until execution and draw conditions are verified and documented.

fields.name: Days 8–14: settlement and ledger readiness
fields.prompt: Define second-week deliverables for agent qualification, contract templates, repayment instructions, ledger setup, and duplicate-event testing. Include a specific mock deal that demonstrates balanced entries without sending real funds to counterparties.
fields.example: By day fourteen, two candidate settlement agents have documented verification files. The team runs LF-030-TEST with $100,000 principal, $2,000 fee, and $400 direct costs. Replaying the release event produces one intent; the mock $102,000 repayment clears both receivables without creating principal revenue.

fields.name: Days 15–21: qualified acquisition pilot
fields.prompt: Set a third-week outreach plan based on eligible counterparties and document completeness. Specify the offer, activity targets, follow-up cadence, and evidence needed before a prospect enters the executable commitment pipeline.
fields.example: The owner contacts ten settlement firms and ten repeat buyers, seeking five complete files rather than twenty verbal promises. Every prospect receives the deposited-cash requirement. Two earnest-money requests lacking end-buyer cash are declined and recorded as ineligible, not counted as lost fundable closings.

fields.name: Days 22–30: rehearsal and readiness review
fields.prompt: Define the final-week rehearsal, evidence review, and conditional first-closing readiness criteria. State how the team will report progress when the first eligible deal arrives after the initial 30-day sprint.
fields.example: The team rehearses a changed-beneficiary incident, a bank timeout, and a three-day repayment delay. Day thirty ends with a signed readiness record and open-items list. If no eligible closing exists, status is launch preparation completed, first deal pending within the stated one-to-four-month window.

fields.name: Small-team responsibility and coverage map
fields.prompt: Allocate work across the canonical staffing models, including independent review and absence coverage. Identify activities requiring specialized external advice and distinguish those engagements from the recurring operating pod headcount.
fields.example: Conservative and base operations use one full-time owner plus two contractors for verification and ledger support. Scaled operations use two full-time staff plus three contractors, five people total. Specialist counsel is purchased as an outside service; its cost must remain inside the modeled expense envelope.

fields.name: Weekly operating KPI scorecard
fields.prompt: Define metrics for eligible pipeline, earned fees, outstanding principal, reserve coverage, settlement duration, exception age, and review quality. Attach a calculation method and action threshold to each metric rather than reporting volume alone.
fields.example: A weekly snapshot shows three eligible files, two completed closings, $4,000 earned fees, and $100,000 principal still outstanding. Protected cash is $50,000. Any unverified release is a zero-tolerance incident; any repayment beyond its contractual deadline receives same-day escalation rather than waiting for the weekly meeting.

fields.name: Scenario tracking and scorecard integrity
fields.prompt: Record canonical scenario targets and the candidate's ranking without presenting them as realized performance. Separate actual results, run-rate estimates, and modeled annual outcomes so the team can investigate variance honestly.
fields.example: Candidate 30 ranks fourth of 36 with 93/100: revenue 25, margin 24, team efficiency 20, startup accessibility 11, and automation 13. Annual owner-profit targets remain $36,000, $227,375, and $522,500. A $4,000 fee week is reported as actual weekly revenue, not proof of the base annual outcome.

fields.name: Growth triggers and capacity expansion
fields.prompt: Specify evidence required before adding facility capacity, counterparties, or headcount. Tie expansion to realized unit economics and reliable controls, and show how scaled throughput differs from the base deployment model.
fields.example: An illustrative scaled stack combines $50,000 deployable equity with an executed $950,000 facility. At 450 closings of $100,000 over two business days, average deployment is $360,000 across 250 business days, or 36% of $1 million capacity. Expansion requires verified demand, clean reconciliations, and modeled facility costs.

fields.name: Continuity and exit-readiness ledger
fields.prompt: List records a successor would need to operate and evaluate the business. Identify transfer restrictions, change-of-control requirements, personal guarantees, and data-access boundaries rather than assuming all assets and relationships transfer automatically.
fields.example: The ledger indexes executed funding contracts, facility covenants, license determinations, agent relationships, bank mandates, and reconciled fee history. Each item records assignment and change-of-control terms. A facility dependent on the owner's personal guarantee is flagged for lender review; its capacity is not represented as automatically transferable.

fields.name: Month-end decision and next commitments
fields.prompt: Summarize completed deliverables, unresolved issues, available capital, and the next 30-day commitments. State precisely which activities may continue and which remain blocked, with accountable owners and dated evidence requirements.
fields.example: The month-end review confirms tested ledger controls, two qualified agent files, and five complete prospect files. External capacity is still unexecuted, so $100,000 commitments remain blocked. The owner continues outreach and contract review while the facility workstream targets documented availability before any larger deal is promised.

worksheets.completion_gate: Close the sprint with a signed evidence register, tested execution controls, exact canonical scenario references, staffed review coverage, and a truthful list of blocked commitments. Authorize the first live advance only when its own underwriting and release requirements are met.
